newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude stuck in range, capped by $24..
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude stuck in range, capped by $24..

text.p: NYMEX crude futures were looking slightly bearish in the short-term, but recent falls did not yet signal the end of the uptrend stretching back to the spring, chartists said.

Jan crude closed 26 cents lower at $23.49 a barrel on Tuesday and was trading one cent higher at $23.50 on ACCESS, while Dec heat closed 0.56 cent off at 72.23 cents a gallon and was trading 0.03 cent lower at 72.20 cents.
"We're suggesting weakness in the short-term in choppy conditions," said Omar Gadsby at MCM in London.
Gadsby saw the parametres of last Wednesday's outside day spanning $23.30 to $24.55 acting as key support and resistance levels.
"The fact it failed to get above $24.55 gave some cause for concern," he said.
"$23.20 is very important support. If it falls below there we could see it heading for the $22.30 level," he said.
In between there, Gadsby saw interim levels at the 62.8 percent retracement of the move up from November 6 to 20 coming in at $23.15 and below there at $23.05.
Gadsby saw key resistance at $23.95 and then $24.55.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International was also bearish in the short-term.

"Resistance around $23.95-$24.01 is the main barrier protecting $24.55 until $23.20 support breaks. Focus shifted to going under $22.25 if $23.13 support is broken on Tuesday as desired," he said in his Global Energy Outlook.

Heating oil also looked set for some choppy range trading with the confines of the highs and lows of last Wednesday's outside day -- coming in at 72 to 75.10 cents for the December contract which expires on Wednesday and 71.48 to 74.40 cents for the January contract.
"Stay bearish short term. Monday's 73.30 high ought to stay intact Tuesday," said Graham.
The 14-day RSI for the January contract was neutral at 54 percent at Monday's close.
